subject: Partner request: feature-flag cohorting + SDK deprecation window
messages:
From: Kenny Park <kenny.park@blueforge.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Request: partner-safe SDK flags + deprecation grace window

Hi Jonas / Vanessa,

Thanks again for the recent demo — BlueForge is close to shipping a major release that embeds the Redwood client SDK across our orchestration layer. Our integrations team found a few upcoming API/SDK changes in your roadmap that would affect our release. We wanted to formally request 1) a partner-friendly feature-flag mechanism (cohort gating) in the SDK/API and 2) an extended deprecation window for breaking changes to model selection and streaming semantics.

Summary of asks (high level):
- Feature flag / cohorting: a server-controlled opt-in flag (per-tenant) that lets us enable new behavior (e.g., modelVariant selection + streaming changes) for a subset of customers for canary testing. Ideally exposed via the SDK so our customers do not need to change application code paths during rollout.
- Back-compat tolerance: SDK client should ignore unknown top-level response fields and continue to work if minor response shape additions are made.
- Deprecation window: we need a 9-month minimum grace period before sunsetting old behaviour for any change that requires BlueForge to ship a breaking client update. This is due to our channel/customer cadence.

Attachments: BlueForge has attached a short spec (blueforge_sdk_change_request.pdf) describing the rollout model we run and a proposed API shape for a feature-flag header (X-Redwood-Feature-Cohort) and suggested semver semantics.

We understand there are product constraints; happy to sync and collaborate on compromise timelines. Our next release branch cut is Oct 4, so a decision within the next 2–3 weeks would be ideal.

Thanks,
Kenny
Kenny Park
Head of Integrations | BlueForge Labs
--
BlueForge Labs | integrations@blueforge.com
From: jonas_weber@redwood.ai
To: Kenny Park <kenny.park@blueforge.com>
Cc: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 10 Sep 2026 10:01:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: partner-safe SDK flags + deprecation grace window

Kenny — thanks for the clear spec and attachment, I skimmed the PDF and it's helpful. Quick notes from product/partnership side:

- We can support a per-tenant server-side cohort flag; engineering already has an internal opt-in gating mechanism for experiments. Exposing it through the SDK as a transparent toggle is reasonable, though we need to decide whether it will be a header, a token-scoped flag, or both.
- Back-compat tolerance: our guideline is "ignore unknown response fields" in SDKs but we will validate the exact surface for each language.
- Deprecation window: our public policy is 6 months for breaking changes, but we can discuss a partner extension for signed deals.

Action items I propose:
1) Engineering to review BlueForge PDF and produce a minimal API changelog diff (we'll attach a draft patch).
2) Schedule a 30-min technical sync next week to align on the header approach and the rollout cadence.
3) I'll escalate the 9-month request to product leadership for an exception; if approved we can capture it as an amendment to the partner addendum.

Proposed sync: Tue, Sep 14 at 11:00 PT — does that work for your team?

I'll attach a small patch that demonstrates a conservative API change and how the SDK could check for the cohort header (api-changelog-diff.patch).

— Jonas
Jonas Weber
Director, Partner Integrations | Redwood Inference
From: vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
To: Kenny Park <kenny.park@blueforge.com>, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 11 Sep 2026 09:30:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: partner-safe SDK flags + deprecation grace window

Kenny, thanks for the detailed ask and the example header. A few product constraints to call out so expectations are clear before the sync: 

- Bandwidth: Engineering has two feature sprints already scheduled in Sep/Oct; we can prioritize a lightweight SDK toggle but a full-language rollout will take time.
- Release gating: we prefer to offer a platform-level flag (server-side) + SDK helper that exposes the flag. Fully embedding the flag in all client SDKs in a non-breaking way will be incremental.
- Deprecation policy: our standard public policy is 6 months; however, for named partners on contract we can support extended timelines as a paid support add-on. We can offer a 7-month standard partner exception right away, and escalate to legal for a 9-month contractual amendment if needed.

Where we can be concrete now:
- Redwood can produce a canary SDK build for BlueForge within 3 weeks after the technical sync.
- We'll provide a platform toggle (tenant-level) gated by the account id; SDKs will expose a flag-check API rather than silently change behavior.

Please come to the sync with your desired canary cohort sizes and test matrix. We'll loop in Marissa for rollout coordination and Marcus on compatibility testing.

Thanks,
Vanessa Ortiz
Sr. Product Manager, Integrations | Redwood Inference
From: Kenny Park <kenny.park@blueforge.com>
To: jonas_weber@redwood.ai, vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, marcus_lin@redwood.ai
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 15:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Request: partner-safe SDK flags + deprecation grace window

All — thanks for the fast responses and the proposed plan. We are OK with the compromise Vanessa outlined (7-month standard partner exception + contractual option for 9 months). Confirming the sync for Tue Sep 14 11:00 PT (I'll send a calendar invite).

Pre-sync deliverables from BlueForge:
- Integration test matrix (matrix.csv) covering our three major supported customers.
- A short list of SDK languages we need prioritized (Node, Python, Java).

Redwood deliverables requested before the meeting:
- A short engineering note describing how the cohort header will be exposed (header vs token) and whether the platform toggle will be account-scoped.
- A canary SDK binary or build plan and an ETA for the canary (ideally within 3 weeks of the sync).

If we can get the above items in the next 10 business days, BlueForge will lock our October release schedule around the canary. We're attaching the integration spec to the invite.

Thanks again, looking forward to the sync.
Kenny
--
Kenny Park | BlueForge Labs
